attributes.body_ja:
「ことになる」は、名詞（めいし）を作（つく）る「こと」と格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」、そして五段動詞（ごだんどうし）の「なる」を合（あ）わせた表現（ひょうげん）です。何（なに）かが、ある状態（じょうたい）や結果（けっか）になることを表（あらわ）します。この表現（ひょうげん）は、主（おも）に自分（じぶん）の意思（いし）とは関係（かんけい）しないところで、物事（ものごと）が決（き）まるようなときに使（つか）われます。

「ことになる」は、主（おも）に、動詞（どうし）やイ形容詞（けいようし）の連体形（れんたいけい）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。また、「な」が付いたナ形容詞（けいようし）に使（つか）われることもあります。

「ことになる」は「(A) に決（き）まる」という意味（いみ）で、ほかの誰（だれ）かの判断（はんだん）や決定（けってい）を表（あらわ）すこともあります。この意味（いみ）になるのは、動詞（どうし）と一緒に使（つか）うときです。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「ことになる」は、「なる」が「する」の自動詞（じどうし）だと言（い）われる理由（りゆう）が見（み）える、良（よ）い例（れい）でしょう。「ことになる」は、自分（じぶん）の判断（はんだん）を表（あらわ）す「ことにする」と違（ちが）って、ほかの誰（だれ）かの判断（はんだん）を表（あらわ）すときによく使（つか）われるからです。「なる」の文（ぶん）の焦点（しょうてん）は、「どのような結果（けっか）になったか」にあります。
attributes.body:
ことになる is an expression that combines the nominalizing use of こと (creating a noun-phrase), with the case marking particle に, and the う - Verb なる 'to become'. This expression can be translated as 'to become (A)', but has the nuance that someone/thing caused (A) to become that way. Due to this, it may also be translated as 'it has been decided that (A)', or 'it will end up being (A)'.

ことになる is primarily used with verbs and い-Adjectives in their attributive form. It may also be used with な-Adjectives followed by な.

The 'it has been decided that (A)' meaning only applies to verbs, as only verbs will be enacted by someone/thing.

Fun Fact

This structure is a good example of why なる is often viewed as the intransitive form of する. する conveys that someone is performing an action (transitive), while なる implies that something is the result of an action (intransitive). This is why the (A) phrase in ことになる is usually determined to have been decided/performed by someone else, while still focusing on exactly 'what' (A) became.

attributes.description: How do ことになる and ようになる differ?
Using 「なる」 and 「する」 with verbs

attributes.body: Both にする and ことになる relate to decisions but differ in agency. にする is used when the speaker actively chooses something, often in daily situations like deciding what to eat, similar to 'I'll go with X.' ことになる, on the other hand, expresses decisions made by others or by circumstance, like saying 'It's been decided that X.'

first_relatable.title: にする
first_relatable.meaning: To decide on, To choose, To make something into, To view something as

second_relatable.title: ことになる
second_relatable.meaning: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that

attributes.body: These expressions are similar in that both are used to express decisions. ことになる conveys that something has been decided or will happen due to external factors, e.g. 来月転勤することになった ('It's been decided that I'll be transferred next month'), while ことにする describes something the speaker has decided of their own power, e.g. 来月仕事を辞めることにした ('I've decided to quit my job next month').

first_relatable.title: ことになる
first_relatable.meaning: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that

second_relatable.title: ことにする
second_relatable.meaning: To decide on, Have decided to

attributes.body: These are closely related patterns with a slight but clear nuance difference. ことになる expresses that something has been decided or will happen, often beyond the speaker's control, e.g. 転勤することになった ('It's been decided that I'll be transferred'), while ことになっている is typically used to refer to an established or habitual rule, e.g. 会議を行うことになっている ('It's been decided we'll hold a meeting').

first_relatable.title: ことになる
first_relatable.meaning: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that

second_relatable.title: ことになっている
second_relatable.meaning: To be expected to, To be scheduled to

attributes.body: These patterns are related in that both center around the idea of something being decided. ことになる expresses that something has been decided or will happen, often beyond the speaker's control, e.g. 転勤することになった ('It's been decided that I'll be transferred'), while に決まっている expresses that something is decisively true, e.g. 勝つに決まっている ('They'll definitely win').

first_relatable.title: ことになる
first_relatable.meaning: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that

second_relatable.title: に決まっている
second_relatable.meaning: Surely, Bound to, Certainly, Be decided

attributes.body: Both ようになる and ことになる express something becoming a certain way, but with different nuances. ようになる describes a change in state, e.g. 話せるようになった ('I became able to speak.') ことになる, on the other hand, conveys a decision made, often outside the speaker's control, e.g. 辞めることになった ('It was decided that I/he/she would quit.').

first_relatable.title: ようになる
first_relatable.meaning: To reach the point that, To come to be that, To turn into

second_relatable.title: ことになる
second_relatable.meaning: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that
